sentences.text: Gorgonichthys is an extinct, monospecific genus of large arthrodire placoderm.
This creature belongs to the order Arthrodira and is classified within the unranked family Aspinothoracidi.
With a headshield length of up to 70 centimeters, Gorgonichthys is estimated to have been comparable in total size to Dunkleosteus.
Fossil specimens include infragnatal plates, or lower jaws, that are scaled against a 1-liter water bottle measuring approximately 23 cm in height.
Fossils of Gorgonichthys were found in the Upper Famennian Cleveland Shales of Ohio, and the type species is Gorgonichthys clarki, described by Claypole in 1892.
A 2022 study by Jobbins et al. suggests Gorgonichthys is more closely related to Heintzichthys than Gymnotrachelus, potentially making it a member of the family Selenosteidae.
Gorgonichthys lived during the Late Devonian period, specifically the Upper Famennian, between 372.15 and 358.86 million years ago.
